**Klynge SYD** is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] in Denmark [^src3] [^src5]. It is systematically monitored in the national quality reports published by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP), which evaluate the clinical treatment and outcomes of patients with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] [^src1] [^src2].

The cluster is notable for meeting the national quality standards for atrial fibrillation care. Specifically, Klynge SYD is highlighted as one of the health clusters that fulfills the standard for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of treatment, achieving a compliance rate of 92.9% [^src1]. Furthermore, clinical outcome data from the period between July 1, 2018, and June 30, 2019, shows that 94.3% of atrial fibrillation patients in Klynge SYD received [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]], successfully meeting the ≥ 90% national target [^src3]. 

Beyond initial treatment metrics, Klynge SYD is evaluated across a wide range of longitudinal and outcome-based indicators. These include 1-year and 2-year treatment coverage [^src2], 5-year treatment coverage [^src3], annual P-creatinine measurements for patients on DOACs, and the incidence of ischemic stroke ([[indikator-5|Indicator 5]]) [^src4]. The cluster's performance is also tracked regarding severe bleeding within one year of a new diagnosis (Indicator 11) [^src6], as well as the development of heart failure and mortality rates (Indicator 15) [^src7]. Geographic distributions and incidence rates, such as those for stroke, are mapped at the health cluster level, placing Klynge SYD within the broader national benchmarking framework alongside other regional clusters like [[klynge-nord|Klynge NORD]] and [[klynge-midt|Klynge MIDT]] [^src4].
